useCases: Send enquiry confirmations and internal owner notifications from a website.
Deliver account invitations, onboarding messages, and product event emails.
Use delivery events to investigate bounces and maintain message suppression.

inputs: Verified sending domain and authorized API access
Approved templates and message triggering rules
steps: Verify the sending domain and configure protected credentials.
Build templates and trigger messages only from approved events.
Check delivery events, failed sends, and duplicate message prevention.
reviewPoints: Review recipient consent and the purpose of each message.
Confirm secrets and recipient data remain outside client-side code.

workflows: Website enquiry: validated submission → acknowledgement → owner notification.
SaaS onboarding: approved invitation → product email → account activation.
Delivery operations: bounce event → suppression update → exception review.
considerations: Sending limits, rate limits, and feature access depend on the plan.
Domain reputation, recipient quality, and sending practices affect delivery.

name: Notion
tagline: Keep briefs, decisions, and operating knowledge easy to find.
description: Notion provides collaborative pages and structured workspace content, with APIs for authorized integrations. We can organize a team's briefs, campaign knowledge, delivery plans, and operating procedures into a clear workspace. An integration can connect approved records to this knowledge layer, while permissions and ownership keep source information distinguishable from drafts and temporary planning notes.
useCases: Build a campaign knowledge hub with briefs, assets, decisions, and review status.
Create delivery plans and operating procedures for a website or SaaS project.
Synchronize approved project records through an authorized API connection.

inputs: Existing briefs, procedures, and project records
Authorized API scope and update rules
outputs: Organized knowledge pages and structured records
Review workflow and content ownership rules
steps: Define source-of-truth pages, record properties, and workspace navigation.
Create templates and role-appropriate access for the team.
Connect approved integrations and verify update and review behavior.
reviewPoints: Review page access and connection capabilities.
Keep approved knowledge distinct from AI drafts and unverified notes.

workflows: Campaign delivery: brief → task plan → asset review → launch record.
Operations handover: workflow → procedure page → assigned owner.
Knowledge sync: approved source record → authorized API → reviewed workspace update.
considerations: Connections require explicit permissions to the relevant workspace content.
Notion is a knowledge layer; transactional application data may need a separate database.

name: Airtable
tagline: Turn structured records into a usable team workflow.
description: Airtable combines structured records with views, interfaces, and automations for business workflows. We can build a focused workspace for lead tracking, inventory, campaign production, or client delivery when the team needs more structure than a spreadsheet. The design includes field definitions, linked records, permissions, and clear review states so the workspace stays useful as the number of records grows.
useCases: Track enquiries, owners, follow-ups, and pipeline stages in a shared workspace.
Manage inventory or campaign assets with linked records and review status.
Build role-specific interfaces and approved notification automations.

inputs: Existing tables and sample operational records
steps: Model tables and relationships and clean the starting data.
Build interfaces and approval states around the team's real tasks.
Review automation drafts, permissions, and record limits before activation.
reviewPoints: Verify interface permissions and field ownership.
Confirm automation actions and plan limits match expected usage.

workflows: Sales workspace: enquiry → owner assignment → follow-up → stage review.
Creative operations: brief → asset record → approval → publishing handoff.
Inventory control: item record → change request → reviewed update.
considerations: Record limits, automation usage, and permission options depend on the plan.
A complex transactional SaaS product may require a dedicated application backend.

name: Jira
tagline: Turn the company roadmap into owned, trackable delivery.
logoSource: Original Jira product icon linked on https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira (Teamwork Collection Jira image), downloaded without recoloring.
description: Jira gives a growing business a structured place to plan work, assign owners, and track delivery across product, engineering, marketing, and operations. We can create a launch backlog for a new company, define work types and approval states, connect releases to implementation tasks, and build dashboards that make stalled work visible. As the company grows, we can extend the setup with team workflows, dependencies, service handoffs, and API integrations. The result is a practical operating system with clear responsibility and review points, rather than a collection of disconnected task lists.
useCases: Create a company launch project covering brand, website, CRM, acquisition, onboarding, and operating procedures.
Set up an engineering backlog with priorities, acceptance criteria, QA ownership, and release readiness.
Route marketing requests and operational exceptions through a visible intake and approval workflow.
Give founders and team leads an agreed view of delivery risks, blocked work, and overdue commitments.
metrics: Work cycle time: median elapsed time from agreed in-progress state to completion.
On-time completion: items completed by their agreed due date ÷ items due in the same period.
Blocked-work share: open items marked blocked ÷ all open items in the selected project.
Release defect rate: confirmed post-release defects ÷ releases, using a stated observation window.

inputs: Client-owned Atlassian site and project access approved by its administrator.
Team roles, work types, statuses, escalation owners, and a definition of done.
API or OAuth credentials with only the required project access; webhook administration rights where needed.
outputs: Company launch and delivery projects with owned work items and acceptance criteria.
Configured statuses, board views, automation rules, and project dashboards.
Integration field map, webhook handling, operating notes, and administrator handover.
steps: Start with the company launch plan, then create project templates and a small set of understandable statuses.
Configure project permissions and integration scopes; verify a restricted user cannot view or change excluded work.
Connect selected issue events over HTTPS, filter the project scope, and deduplicate retries before updating downstream tools.
Pilot one request-to-completion workflow with the team, review failures, then expand to recurring delivery and reporting.
reviewPoints: Approve workflow ownership, status changes, project access, and release acceptance criteria.
Check duplicate webhook events, failed delivery recovery, and app access before enabling live cross-system updates.

workflows: Company launch: founder roadmap → owned Jira work items → weekly review → verified launch checklist.
Software delivery: feature request → prioritization → implementation → QA → release → support follow-up.
Campaign operations: approved campaign brief → content and tracking tasks → launch review → experiment backlog.
Scaled operations: intake → responsible team → exception escalation → closure → monthly delivery review.
considerations: Automation allowances and advanced planning features depend on the selected Jira plan and configuration.
API scopes do not replace project permissions. An administrator must approve the access model and relevant webhook registration method.
Webhook retries can produce duplicate events; integrations need idempotent handling, failed-delivery review, and periodic reconciliation.
Board data measures the defined workflow; it does not establish employee productivity or guarantee launch success.

name: Asana
tagline: Coordinate the work that takes a business from setup to scale.
logoSource: Current official Asana horizontal logo from https://asana.com/brand, downloaded from the official asset transform as PNG. Symbol and wordmark remain together in their original colors.
description: Asana helps business teams coordinate projects, responsibilities, due dates, and recurring work. We can create an organized workspace for a company launch, marketing calendar, client onboarding, hiring operations, and internal requests. Each process has a template, a responsible person, an agreed deadline, and a review step. For a larger company, we can connect task changes to approved reporting and automation so founders and managers can understand progress without manually collecting updates from every team.
useCases: Build a reusable launch template covering positioning, brand, website, lead capture, sales handoff, and support readiness.
Create a campaign calendar with content owners, dependencies, review stages, and publication dates.
Set up repeatable client onboarding and delivery projects from a scoped agreement to final handover.
Create hiring and employee onboarding checklists with role-specific owners and access requests.
metrics: Milestone completion: completed milestones ÷ milestones due in the chosen period.
Overdue-task share: unfinished past-due tasks ÷ all unfinished tasks with due dates.
Approval turnaround: elapsed time from review request to approved or rejected decision.
Onboarding cycle time: elapsed time from confirmed start to completion of the agreed onboarding checklist.

inputs: Client-owned Asana organization or workspace and approved administrator access.
Project templates, task owners, milestones, due-date rules, and external collaborator requirements.
OAuth application credentials and minimal required scopes; access to every subscribed resource.
outputs: Business launch, campaign, onboarding, and recurring operations templates.
Project ownership rules, task fields, reporting views, and team operating guidance.
Authorized API integration, webhook receiver, reconciliation process, and handover notes.
steps: Map business processes, agree task ownership and due-date rules, then build a template for each recurring workflow.
Configure project visibility, external collaborator access, and minimal OAuth scopes; test with representative roles.
Subscribe to selected task or project changes, complete the webhook secret handshake, and verify incoming signatures.
Run a pilot, handle missing or delayed events with reconciliation where required, and review project metrics with team leads.
reviewPoints: Approve task templates, client visibility, confidential project access, and milestone definitions.
Test authentication expiry, signature verification, webhook failure handling, and periodic state reconciliation.

workflows: Company setup: launch checklist → owners and milestones → weekly progress review → operational handover.
Marketing delivery: campaign brief → asset production → stakeholder review → scheduled publication → learnings.
Client journey: signed scope → onboarding project → delivery milestones → approval → renewal preparation.
Scaled team: recurring operations template → distributed owners → escalation → portfolio review where the plan supports it.
considerations: Rules, reporting, portfolios, and advanced governance depend on the selected plan and feature availability.
Tokens act within the authorized user and resource permissions; never use a broad personal token as an unreviewed company-wide integration.
Webhooks are not a replayable audit ledger and may miss events in exceptional circumstances; reconcile resource state when complete processing is required.
Due dates and completion records require consistent team usage to make the suggested metrics meaningful.

name: Slack
tagline: Bring decisions, alerts, and company handoffs into clear channels.
logoSource: Authentic full-color Slack symbol served by the official Slack asset CDN; brand guidance at https://slack.com/media-kit. Original PNG preserved with adjacent Slack name.
description: Slack connects company conversations with the systems that produce the work. We can create a workspace and channel structure for founders, marketing, sales, engineering, support, and selected client relationships. We can also build approved alerts and interactive app workflows that surface a new enquiry, an overdue task, a deployment issue, or a review request at the right moment. The setup includes channel ownership, access boundaries, notification rules, and a documented route from conversation to a tracked action.
useCases: Set up a new company workspace with launch, decisions, sales, marketing, engineering, and support channels.
Send qualified lead and workflow failure alerts to the assigned team with a link back to the source record.
Build request, approval, and task-creation interactions for authorized internal users.
Connect client collaboration through an approved Slack Connect arrangement and clear internal/external boundaries.
metrics: Alert acknowledgement time: elapsed time from delivered operational alert to recorded owner acknowledgement.
Approval turnaround: elapsed time from a request to the stored approval decision.
Handoff completion: accepted handoffs ÷ handoffs created within the same defined period.
Workflow delivery success: successful required app actions ÷ attempted app actions, measured in integration logs.

inputs: Client-owned Slack workspace and administrator approval for app installation.
Channel map, channel owners, membership boundaries, and event-specific notification rules.
Authorized OAuth app scopes, signing secret, and secure server-side credentials.
outputs: Company channel architecture, onboarding guidance, and communication conventions.
Configured webhook alerts or interactive Slack app connected to approved systems.
Scope inventory, request verification, delivery logs, and support handover.
steps: Create a purposeful channel and ownership structure, then agree which business events should produce notifications.
Install a client-approved app with minimal OAuth scopes and confirm access only to the intended channels.
Use incoming webhooks for simple outbound alerts; use the Web API and Events API for authorized interactive or event-driven behavior.
Verify requests, queue longer actions, respect rate limits, and pilot the complete alert-to-owner workflow before wider rollout.
reviewPoints: Approve app scopes, channel destinations, sensitive data handling, and external collaboration membership.
Test private-channel access, request verification, duplicate events, failed notifications, and escalation ownership.

workflows: Company launch: founder decisions channel → linked Jira or Asana task → owner acknowledgement → launch review.
Sales response: qualified CRM enquiry → assigned-team alert → owner action → CRM status update.
Product operations: deployment or monitoring event → engineering channel → incident owner → tracked resolution.
Client delivery: approved shared channel → scoped request → internal task → review → client update.
considerations: Incoming webhooks post messages to a configured conversation; they do not by themselves read messages or run arbitrary company actions.
OAuth scopes, channel membership, and workspace app approval determine what an integration can access.
Message retention, advanced administration, Slack Connect, and workflow features depend on the plan and organization policy.
API rate limits require throttling and retry handling; notification volume must be tuned so important alerts remain visible.

name: Discord
tagline: Build a structured community around the company and its customers.
logoSource: Original Discord symbol linked by https://discord.com/branding, preserved in its official color and shown beside the Discord name.
description: Discord can provide a community space for a company, customer group, product users, or learning program. We can create a server with clear channels, roles, onboarding guidance, moderation procedures, and a route for feedback and support requests. We can add permitted bots, app commands, and operational notifications so the community connects to the company delivery process. As membership grows, the setup can expand into structured feedback, member support, release announcements, and recurring community activities with human moderation.
useCases: Create a product launch community with onboarding, announcements, questions, feedback, and dedicated support channels.
Configure role-based access for staff, customers, moderators, and invited partners.
Build app commands that capture a structured support request or feature suggestion into an approved task system.
Deliver release and service-status notifications to the intended channels using protected webhooks.
metrics: Onboarding completion: members completing the agreed welcome steps ÷ eligible new members.
Support first-response time: elapsed time from a tracked support request to its first meaningful response.
Feedback resolution: feedback items with a communicated outcome ÷ reviewed feedback items.
Webhook delivery success: successful notification deliveries ÷ attempted deliveries recorded by the integration.

inputs: Client-owned Discord server, administrator approval, and documented community purpose.
Channel structure, role hierarchy, moderation owners, and member onboarding process.
Approved developer application, limited bot permissions, and protected webhook or bot credentials.
outputs: Configured server channels, roles, welcome flow, and moderation operating guide.
Authorized notification webhooks, app commands, and links to the selected delivery system.
Permission checklist, event-processing controls, usage reporting, and administrator handover.
steps: Design the community journey and establish channel owners, roles, and escalation routes.
Configure role and channel permissions, then install only the approved app scopes and bot permissions.
Use an incoming webhook for outbound channel notifications; use application commands or relevant event APIs for supported interactive actions.
Test restricted-role access, validate signed HTTP interactions where used, respect API rate limits, and pilot moderation and support before broad invitations.
reviewPoints: Approve community rules, channel visibility, role permissions, moderation responsibilities, and public information.
Verify that bot actions cannot bypass member access boundaries and that support requests reach an accountable company owner.

workflows: Company launch: invited founding users → welcome steps → feedback channel → prioritized launch improvements.
Customer support: structured request command → approved support queue → owner response → closure communicated to the member.
Product growth: release record → announcement webhook → community questions → tracked follow-up.
Scaled community: role-based segments → scheduled community activity → moderation review → recurring feedback report.
considerations: An incoming webhook is an outbound posting mechanism; it does not grant general access to server conversations.
Bot permissions, channel overrides, OAuth scopes, and applicable privileged intents must be reviewed against the intended use.
Rate limits, token protection, and human moderation are required for dependable operation.
A community server is not the authoritative store for billing, customer consent, or company records; retain those records in the chosen business system.
